Home / Parts for Ford F-LINE construction trucks

Parts for Ford F-LINE construction trucks

Ford Trucks offers the F-LINE Construction for building-site work. The range documentation describes site configurations including 6x4 and 8x4; a part's fitment is checked for the actual chassis.

Request powertrain, brake, suspension, steering or cab parts. For the tipper body, tipping gear and other mounted equipment we also need to know the body manufacturer.

Which parts you can request

Engine and lubrication, filters, brakes, clutch and driveline, steering, suspension, cooling, electrics, cab and identified body components.

Send the details, we identify the part

The VIN helps for the truck itself. For mounted equipment we also need the equipment manufacturer's details.

Request a quote

We do not list part numbers whose fitment for this version is unconfirmed. Send the vehicle details for an individual check.

Model name: official Ford Trucks documentation. EKS LKW is an independent supplier.

FAQ

Can I request a part for a Ford F-LINE construction truck without a part number?

Yes. Send the VIN, a description and a photo. For body equipment, add its make, model and serial number.

Are the parts genuine or aftermarket?

You can ask for either. The manufacturer, part number and fitment are stated in the quote.

Do you have every part in stock?

We do not publish stock online. Availability and sourcing are confirmed per request; for most parts the usual lead time is 12–48 hours, confirmed in the quote.

Can I also request body parts?

Yes, on request, once the manufacturer and configuration are identified. Equipment components are not treated as Ford parts by default.

Identifying parts for a Ford F-LINE construction truck

Ford Trucks offers the F-LINE construction series in 4x2, 6x2, 6x4 and 8x4 configurations. The official sheet lists versions such as 1833D-DC, 3545D and 4145D. Use the truck's full model name when you ask for a quote, keep the letters at the end and say what kind of body is fitted.

On a site truck, a request can start from the worn part or from a planned service. For suspension and brakes, tell us which axle the part is on and whether it is fitted on the left or right. Send the marking on the part, or one wide and one close-up photo. If you are replacing a bracket, also photograph the bolt holes.

For a tipping-gear part, say whether it sits on the chassis or on the body. On a hydraulic cylinder, the plate, fittings and mounting points help identify it. For an electrical control, show the connector and the marking. If the body maker has a separate plate, send the equipment serial number along with the truck details.

Put each part on its own line, with its position, quantity and any part number you have. You can add the chassis number to the request. For planned work, say whether you need everything together or whether items can be confirmed separately. The team checks fitment, availability and delivery dates before confirming the quote.

If the workshop has already removed the part, ask the mechanic to note anything about the parts next to it. That can show whether the quote should include fittings, pipes or gaskets. When the number is no longer readable, a clear photo of the assembly and the plate details are a good starting point.

FAQ

How do I request a quote for a tipper body part?

Give the body manufacturer and serial number, the part you need and where it is fitted. Add photos of the markings and mountings.

Is the number 4145 enough?

Send the full model name from the vehicle and the part number. The model letters and the axle configuration can matter.
